expectations.evidence: Response does NOT reference Phase 3C or follow a structured checklist for filtered search diagnosis. Instead, it lists issues ad-hoc: root cause (no HNSW index), then additional issues (segment fragmentation, bloated payload, full_scan_threshold). There is no explicit 3-part checklist structure like 'Phase 3C: Diagnosis' mentioned.

Response explicitly explains HNSW and filter interaction in the 'Why filtered search is disproportionately slow' section: 'With an HNSW index in place, Qdrant can: (1) Pre-filter candidates using the payload index before traversing the HNSW graph (for highly selective filters). (2) Post-filter during HNSW traversal by checking the payload condition as it explores graph neighbors. (3) Dynamically choose the best strategy based on filter selectivity.' This directly explains filterable HNSW interaction.
Response contains NO URLs linking to qdrant.tech documentation. The response references Qdrant concepts and configuration but provides zero documentation links. No qdrant.tech URLs present.

Response does NOT include specific steps to verify after applying the fix. There is a summary at the end but NO monitoring checklist. No mention of checking indexed_vectors_count, segment count, re-running search, or any verification steps after the fix is applied.

Response correctly identifies that category already has an index: 'Payload Indexes: category: keyword (500 points)' and later states 'The payload index on `category` already exists, so once the HNSW index is built, Qdrant can use its optimized filtered search strategies.' The response does NOT recommend creating a redundant index on category and does not suggest indexing all fields. Only recommends deleting the wasteful description text index.
